actions.summary: The actions mostly point to long-planned steps to make European households and reserve forces more resilient to disruption and to a possible future confrontation with Russia. Asian governments, meanwhile, are working to calm supply fears from the Hormuz fighting. Few of today's steps are sudden: Israel's shelter opening and Moldova's reported martial-law bill are the main new short-notice items, and the Moldovan item rests on Russian state media. Overall confidence that these steps point to a specific near-term threat is low to moderate.

patterns.title: European governments roll out 72-hour household self-sufficiency campaigns
patterns.points_to: Together these steps prepare households to get through several days without normal power, water, payments or transport. That disruption could come from sabotage, cyberattacks or a wider crisis, as well as from storms or floods.
patterns.unsaid: The run of airport drone incidents, cable damage and cyber warnings, alongside warnings from defence chiefs, suggests governments see deliberate hybrid disruption as a main driver. Most campaigns still describe their aim in general all-hazards terms.
patterns.plain_explanation: Most of these steps follow the EU's March 2025 Preparedness Union Strategy and national campaigns announced months or years earlier. The October–November cluster mostly reflects those programmes reaching households, and local reminders like Terschelling's are routine.

patterns.title: Reservist and mobilisation steps around Russia's western border
patterns.points_to: Poland, Norway, Finland and Moldova are making reserves easier to train and call up. Moldova's steps also include legal groundwork for martial law, as reported via Russian and Belarusian outlets. On Russia's side, Verstka reports Rosgvardia is preparing for mobilisation in advance. Together these point to building the ability to expand forces quickly over a period of years, not to a set date.
patterns.unsaid: The steps are consistent with governments planning for the Dutch and German assessments that Russia could test NATO after fighting in Ukraine stops. They may also be planning for Moldova as an exposed point. On Russia's side, a reported 'no second wave' statement of unclear date sits next to quiet preparations reported by Verstka.
patterns.plain_explanation: Nordic and Polish reserve reforms have been under way since 2022 and are largely budget-driven. Moldova's bill may be overdue legal tidying of wartime rules. Only Russian and Belarusian outlets have reported it so far, and they may frame it to provoke worry.

That concern has risen as the Hormuz fighting flares again: two tankers hit mines, and the IRGC claims tanker fires.
